Google becomes Wall Street's top media dog - ABC News

# Google becomes Wall Street's top media dog

Posted Tue 7 Jun 2005 at 6:47pm Tue 7 Jun 2005 at 6:47pm Tue 7 Jun 2005 at 6:47pm, updated Tue 7 Jun 2005 at 7:41pm Tue 7 Jun 2005 at 7:41pm Tue 7 Jun 2005 at 7:41pm

Google ... now more valuable than Time Warner. (Reuters)

Wall Street has determined that Google is the most valuable media company on the planet.

The company's shares, which went public in August at $US75, rose $US10.68 on Monday to close at $US290.94.

Yahoo Finance says that gives the new media youngster a market capitalisation of $US80.8 billion.

Shares of Time Warner, which until Monday was considered the world's biggest media company, dropped 23 cents to $US17.02, giving the company a $US79.8 billion market cap.

Google's stock performance has been extraordinary of late, harkening back to the Internet bubble days, with one important difference: profit.

An analyst with RBC Capital Markets says Google could earn about $US1 billion this year and more than $US2.5 billion in 2007.

Even before Monday's rise of Google shares, pundits were noting the runaway nature of the company's market cap, making such observations as Google being worth more than the Walt Disney Company and General Motors combined, or more than the combined value of Dow Jones & Co and the New York Times Company.

That Google's worth would cruise past that of Time Warner is ironic because the latter sports an asset that once was considered the gold standard of the Internet - America Online.

In January 2000, when Time Warner said it would merge with the world's most richly valued new-media company at the time, AOL had a market cap that towered over Time Warner, the world's most richly valued traditional media company, by $US164 billion to $US83 billion.

Time Warner today is worth less with AOL than it was worth without it, prompting some analysts to posit that - in light of Wall Street valuing what is now a very profitable AOL as an asset worth somewhere between zero and just $US8 billion - it might be time to buy Time Warner shares again.

Of course, market caps are fluid and any downturn in Google shares - or uptick in Time Warner's - could easily make Google the world's second-biggest media company.

Revenue is another measure of a company's size.

By that standard, Time Warner, with about $US42.4 billion in annual revenue, dwarfs Google's roughly $US3.8 billion yearly revenue.

- Reuters
